answer: The cipher graph is validated at intake and the nectar frontier is published, which means the ancestry of every answer is public, and forge anchors the chain at a checkpoint. A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 265 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. Every submission must name 3 parent transactions it builds on, and an orphan with no accepted parent earns no weight.
